description: Calendar hub: every calendar repo, approach and visual style in this toolkit, with when to use it, when not to, and how to integrate it. Source of truth for docs/calendars/catalog.md and the site's Calendars page. Edit here, then run node scripts/build.mjs.

licenses.name: Permissive
licenses.meaning: MIT, Apache-2.0 or BSD. Use in any project. Keep the license notice.

licenses.name: File copyleft
licenses.meaning: MPL-2.0. Use as a dependency freely; changes to its own files must stay open.

licenses.name: Copyleft
licenses.meaning: GPL or AGPL. Study it, run it as a separate service, or fork it as open source. Do not paste its code into a closed client app.

licenses.name: Look only
licenses.meaning: No license or all rights reserved. Read it for ideas; do not copy code.

statuses.meaning: No meaningful updates for 2+ years. Learn from it; prefer a maintained option for production.
Officially shut down or replaced by its authors.

categories.name: Calendar UI components
categories.blurb: Draw month, week, agenda and picker views inside your own app.

categories.name: Complete calendar apps
categories.blurb: Finished calendar products to study, self-host or fork.

categories.name: Provider APIs & SDKs
categories.blurb: Read and write real calendars (Google, CalDAV, Outlook) from your backend.

categories.name: Agent & automation
categories.blurb: Let an AI agent or a script check availability and manage events.

categories.name: Sync & interoperability
categories.blurb: Move events between systems: ICS files, recurrence rules, Outlook to Google.

categories.name: Meetings & video
categories.blurb: Video rooms, meeting grids and join links that attach to events.

styles.name: Month grid
styles.summary: Six-week grid with event chips. The default answer to 'show me my month'.
use_when: Planning across weeks
Events are mostly all-day or few per day
avoid_when: More than 3 timed events a day; use Week
rules: Show 6 rows so the grid never jumps height
Today gets a filled marker, selected day a ring
Overflow becomes '+2 more', never a scroll inside a cell
Arrow keys move between days (roving tabindex)

styles.name: Week time grid
styles.summary: Hours down the side, days across. Overlapping events sit side by side.
use_when: Timed meetings and calls
Finding gaps in a day
avoid_when: Phones under 400px wide; switch to 3-day or Agenda
rules: All-day lane above the hours
Current-time line only on today, updated once a minute while visible
Event height = duration; min height fits one line
Scroll to working hours on open

styles.name: Agenda list
styles.summary: Upcoming events grouped by day. Best on phones and in a Today view.
use_when: Phones
Today / This week cards on a dashboard
Screen readers (a list is the most accessible calendar)
avoid_when: Spotting free time; use Week
rules: Sticky day headers
Time, title, who: in that order
Empty days are skipped, with 'Nothing else this week' at the end

styles.name: Date and range picker
styles.summary: Mini month for choosing a date or a range inside a form.
use_when: Due dates, follow-up dates, report ranges
Booking check-in / check-out
avoid_when: Dates far in the past (birthdays); a typed field is faster
rules: Typed input always works too
Range shows start, end and the days between
Disabled dates explain why on focus
Enter selects, Escape closes, focus returns to the field

styles.name: Year heatmap
styles.summary: One square per day, shaded by activity. Shows rhythm over a year.
use_when: Activity history (calls, sessions, sales) over months
avoid_when: Exact values matter; pair with a number or a tooltip
rules: Sequential palette from one hue
Every square focusable or summarized in text
Legend with the actual ranges

styles.name: Booking slots
styles.summary: Pick a day, then a free time. The visitor's time zone is shown and changeable.
use_when: Clients booking a call with you
Discovery calls from a website
avoid_when: Internal scheduling between colleagues; use free/busy in Week
rules: Only free slots are shown; nothing to fail later
Time zone visible and editable
Confirm step summarizes before booking
Sends a calendar invite with the video link

styles.name: Week strip
styles.summary: A swipeable row of days with dots, above a list of that day's events.
use_when: Phone-first apps
Day-at-a-time workflows (appointments, classes)
avoid_when: Desktop planning; use Month or Week
rules: Dots show 'has events', not counts
Selected day stays centred
Buttons for previous / next week as well as swipe

styles.name: Meeting grid
styles.summary: Equal tiles for every participant, speaker highlighted. For video meeting UIs.
use_when: Building a video room or a meeting recap screen
avoid_when: Meetings are better handled by Meet or Zoom links; don't build video unless it is the product
rules: Tiles keep 16:9 and reflow by count
Speaker highlight uses a ring, not size change (no layout shift)
Names always visible; initials when video is off

approaches.name: Build the view from tokens
approaches.when: You need one simple view (agenda card, mini month) in a dashboard and want it to match the theme exactly.
approaches.not_when: You need drag-to-reschedule, recurring events or resource views; use a library.

approaches.name: Calendar UI library
approaches.when: You need full Month/Week/Day views with drag and drop in a web or mobile app.
approaches.not_when: A small read-only list is enough.

approaches.name: Provider API (Google Calendar v3)
approaches.when: Events must appear in the client's real Google calendar, with invites and Meet links.
approaches.not_when: Calendar data never leaves your app; store it in your own database.

approaches.name: Agent connector (MCP)
approaches.when: An AI assistant should check availability, draft events or summarize the week.
approaches.not_when: The action must run unattended without a human approving it.

approaches.name: Self-hosted CalDAV
approaches.when: The client wants their calendar off Google, on their own server.

approaches.name: ICS feed or file
approaches.when: People should subscribe to your app's events in any calendar app (Google, Apple, Outlook) with no login.
approaches.not_when: Changes must sync both ways; feeds are read-only and refresh slowly.

approaches.name: Sync bridge
approaches.when: Someone lives in Outlook at work and Google at home and needs both to match.
approaches.not_when: You control both sides; write to one calendar and invite the other.

approaches.name: Booking page
approaches.when: Clients pick their own time for a call.

approaches.name: Video meetings
approaches.when: Each event needs a join link.
approaches.not_when: Never build your own video stack for a CRM. Attach a Google Meet link through the Calendar API.

repos.name: Calendar (kizitonwose)
repos.summary: Logic-only calendar for Android Views and Compose Multiplatform. You draw every cell; it handles weeks, months, years, ranges and a heatmap mode.
use_when: Native Android or Compose Multiplatform app
You want a fully custom look (week strip, heatmap, range picker)
avoid_when: Web or React Native projects
integrate: Add the compose or view artifact from Maven Central
Start from the sample app's closest example (week, month, heatmap)
Map design tokens to Compose theme colors; draw day cells with them
repos.learn_from: Separate date logic from rendering. The library owns the calendar math, you own every pixel.

repos.name: CalendarView (huanghaibin)
repos.summary: Canvas-drawn Android calendar built for speed and low memory, with many prebuilt styles (Chinese lunar dates, ranges, multi-select).
use_when: Android app that needs a fast, styled month view with lunar or marker support
avoid_when: You need the iOS-style vertical/horizontal switch: that part is closed source after 3.7.1
Compose-first apps; prefer kizitonwose
integrate: implementation 'com.haibin:calendarview:3.7.1' (AndroidX)
Subclass MonthView / WeekView and draw with Canvas
Follow QUESTION.md for the English docs
repos.learn_from: Drawing on a canvas instead of nested views keeps scrolling smooth with many markers.

repos.name: JTAppleCalendar
repos.summary: UIKit calendar where you design every date cell. Range selection, month/week switching, custom headers.
use_when: UIKit iOS app needing a custom calendar
avoid_when: SwiftUI-first apps (use SwiftUI's DatePicker or a SwiftUI calendar)
Cross-platform projects; use react-native-calendars
integrate: Swift Package Manager or CocoaPods
Read docs/get-started in the repo (the wiki link is down)
Build a cell class that reads colors from your token mapping
repos.learn_from: Week and month are the same grid with a different row count; switch by changing rows, not views.

repos.name: React Native Calendars (Wix)
repos.summary: Pure-JS calendar, agenda, week strip and timeline components for iOS and Android with dot, multi-dot and period marking.
use_when: Expo or React Native app
Mobile companion to a web CRM (Today agenda, week strip)
avoid_when: Web-only projects (it targets native)
integrate: npm i react-native-calendars
Pass a theme object built from tokens (calendarBackground, todayTextColor, selectedDayBackgroundColor…)
Use AgendaList + ExpandableCalendar for a Today screen; markedDates for status dots
repos.learn_from: Marking styles (dot, multi-dot, period) cover almost every 'what's on this day' need without custom cells.

repos.name: rc-calendar
repos.summary: The React calendar and picker that older Ant Design versions used. Date, month, year and decade panels, week numbers. Built on moment.js.
use_when: Maintaining an existing app that already depends on it
avoid_when: New projects: it depends on moment.js; use react-day-picker (shadcn Calendar) instead
integrate: Prefer migrating to react-day-picker
If you must keep it: wrap it and restyle with token CSS variables
repos.learn_from: Panel drill-down (day → month → year → decade) is a fast way to jump far in time.

repos.name: Nextcloud Calendar
repos.summary: Full calendar app for Nextcloud: CalDAV sync, attendees, free/busy, reminders, appointment booking and Talk rooms. Built on FullCalendar and ical.js.
use_when: Client wants a self-hosted calendar off Google
Studying a complete, accessible calendar UX (free/busy, attendees, booking)
avoid_when: Embedding code into a closed client app (AGPL)
Nobody can maintain a Nextcloud server
integrate: Install from the Nextcloud app store on the client's server
Your app talks to it over CalDAV (tsdav or cdav-library), not by importing its code
repos.learn_from: Free/busy next to the attendee list is the clearest way to pick a meeting time.

repos.name: Fossify Calendar
repos.summary: Private, ad-free Android calendar: day, week, month, year and event-list views, CalDAV sync, widgets and themes.
use_when: Studying a polished mobile calendar with every view
Recommending a private calendar app to a client
avoid_when: Copying code into a closed-source app (GPL)
integrate: Use as a reference for view switching and widget design
Clients can sync it with Google or Nextcloud via CalDAV
repos.learn_from: One app, five views, one consistent event chip. The chip design carries across every view.

repos.name: Google Calendar MCP (nspady)
repos.summary: MCP server that gives an AI assistant Google Calendar tools: multi-account, multi-calendar listing, conflict detection, free/busy, recurring edits and event import from images or PDFs.
use_when: An agent should check availability or draft events across several Google accounts
Building or testing calendar features with Claude
avoid_when: The hosted Google Calendar connector already covers the need
Unattended writes; keep a human approval step
integrate: Create a Google Cloud project, enable Calendar API, make a Desktop OAuth client
Add the server to your MCP config with the credentials path
Start read-only; allow create/update once the approval flow is in place
repos.learn_from: Conflict detection across accounts is the feature people actually want from a calendar assistant.

repos.name: gcalcli
repos.summary: Google Calendar from the terminal: agenda, week and month text views, search, quick-add, ICS import, conflict finding and reminder hooks.
use_when: Scripts and agents in a terminal need calendar access
Seeding test events or importing ICS during development
avoid_when: Production app features; call the API from your backend instead
integrate: pipx install gcalcli; run gcalcli init for OAuth
gcalcli agenda --tsv for machine-readable output
Use in dev scripts, not in the deployed app
repos.learn_from: A text agenda proves the minimum useful calendar: time, title, calendar color.

repos.name: laravel-google-calendar (Spatie)
repos.summary: Eloquent-style Event model for Google Calendar in Laravel: create, list, update, delete, add attendees and a Meet link in a few lines.
use_when: The backend is Laravel
A service account or OAuth calendar should mirror app bookings
avoid_when: Next.js / Node stacks (use googleapis for Node)
integrate: composer require spatie/laravel-google-calendar
Service account JSON in env, share the calendar with the service account email
$event->addMeetLink() for video calls
repos.learn_from: Treat the external calendar like a model: new Event, set fields, save(). That's the API shape to copy in any stack.

repos.name: googleapis (API definitions)
repos.summary: Google's public API definitions. Has the Meet REST API (google/apps/meet/v2: spaces, conference records, transcripts) and the Workspace Events API (google/apps/events) for push subscriptions. Calendar v3 itself is a REST API documented separately, not in this repo.
use_when: Reading Meet conference records, participants or transcripts after a call
Subscribing to Workspace events instead of polling
avoid_when: Plain calendar work; use the Calendar v3 REST client (googleapis npm package)
integrate: Don't clone it into the app; use the generated client libraries
Read google/apps/meet/v2/resource.proto to learn the conference record shape
Use the Workspace Events API to get pushed meeting events
repos.learn_from: Meeting data (who joined, transcript) and calendar data (when, who's invited) are separate APIs. Join them on the event's Meet code.

repos.name: Outlook Google Calendar Sync
repos.summary: Free Windows tool that syncs Outlook and Google calendars one or both ways, including attendees and reminders. Works behind proxies, no install required.
use_when: A client keeps a work Outlook and a personal Google calendar and the CRM reads Google
avoid_when: Mac-only users
You can use Microsoft Graph directly from the backend
integrate: Client installs it on their Windows PC
Point it at the Google calendar your app reads
Document it in the handover guide; it's a user tool, not app code
repos.learn_from: Sync tools need clear direction (one-way vs two-way) and a dry-run. Show both in any sync settings UI.

repos.name: Google Calendar for Chrome
repos.summary: Retired extension (5M+ users) that showed upcoming events in a toolbar popup and added events from any page. Source kept for forking.
use_when: Studying the quick-glance popup pattern for 'what's next'
avoid_when: Shipping it as-is: it is retired and uses an old extension manifest
integrate: Use as a design reference only
If a client wants a 'next meeting' popup, build it on Manifest V3 with the Calendar API
repos.learn_from: The most-used calendar view is 'next 3 events'. Put that on the dashboard's Today panel.

repos.name: Video Meeting (0x5eba)
repos.summary: Small peer-to-peer video room (React, Node, Socket.IO, WebRTC) with chat and screen sharing, no accounts.
use_when: Learning how WebRTC signalling works
avoid_when: Production meetings: no license, no TURN server setup, peer-to-peer breaks past a few people
A CRM: attach Google Meet or Zoom links instead
integrate: Read only. For real video use a hosted SDK (Zoom Video SDK, LiveKit, Daily) or Meet links
repos.learn_from: Equal tiles plus a chat drawer is the minimum meeting layout.

repos.name: Google Meet clone (ckalgos)
repos.summary: Tutorial video-conference app with Firebase signalling, screen sharing and a responsive grid for 8 to 12 people.
use_when: Studying responsive meeting grids for desktop and mobile
avoid_when: Copying code (no license)
Production video
integrate: Reference only for grid layout at different participant counts
repos.learn_from: Grid columns step with participant count (1, 2, 4, 9, 12) so tiles stay large.

repos.name: Google Meet Grid View
repos.summary: Former extension that forced an equal-tile grid in Google Meet, with speaker highlight and 'hide no-video' options. Meet now has this built in.
use_when: Reference for meeting-grid options: include yourself, highlight speaker, hide tiles without video
avoid_when: Using the code (all rights reserved)
Modern Meet already has tiled layout
integrate: Copy the ideas, not the code: the three toggles make a good meeting-recap view
repos.learn_from: Highlight the speaker with a border, never by resizing, so nothing jumps.

repos.name: Google Meet Scheduler
repos.summary: Bot that logs into Google with a stored password and joins Meet calls on a schedule using browser automation. Windows only.
use_when: As an example of what not to build
avoid_when: Always for client work: it stores a Google password in a file, automates login (against Google's terms) and acts without a person
integrate: Don't. To get meeting notes, use a recorder connector (Fathom, Fireflies) or the Meet REST API with OAuth
repos.learn_from: Automation must use OAuth and an approval step, never stored passwords.

repos.name: React DayPicker (shadcn Calendar)
repos.summary: Accessible date and range picker. It is what shadcn/ui's Calendar component wraps, so it fits this toolkit's stack with no extra styling work.
use_when: Any date or range input in a Next.js + shadcn app
A mini month on a dashboard sidebar
avoid_when: Full week/day scheduling with drag; use FullCalendar or Schedule-X
integrate: npx shadcn@latest add calendar (installs react-day-picker)
It already reads the shadcn CSS variables mapped in design-system/tailwind.preset.js
Use mode="range" for report filters; disabled for past dates
repos.learn_from: Keyboard grid navigation and ARIA come built in. Don't rebuild them by hand.

repos.name: FullCalendar
repos.summary: The most widely used web calendar: month, week, day and list views, drag to move or resize, Google Calendar and ICS sources. Resource timelines are a paid add-on.
use_when: Full scheduling screen in a web app (bookings, team calendar)
Showing a Google calendar or ICS feed inside the app
avoid_when: You need resource/timeline views and no budget for the premium license
A simple agenda card
integrate: npm i @fullcalendar/react @fullcalendar/daygrid @fullcalendar/timegrid @fullcalendar/interaction
Theme it by setting its --fc-* CSS variables from design tokens
Load events on open and on change (eventSources function), never on a timer
repos.learn_from: Event sources as functions (fetch for the visible range) keep big calendars fast.

repos.name: Schedule-X
repos.summary: Modern Material-style event calendar for React, Vue, Svelte, Angular or plain JS, with drag and drop, dark mode and plugins.
use_when: You want a clean modern look with less CSS work than FullCalendar
avoid_when: You depend on FullCalendar's larger plugin ecosystem
integrate: npm i @schedule-x/react @schedule-x/calendar @schedule-x/theme-default
Override its CSS variables with design tokens
Use the events service plugin to add or update events from your store
repos.learn_from: Good defaults for dark mode come from one set of variables. Same idea as our themes.

repos.name: Google Calendar API v3
repos.summary: The official API behind every Google calendar integration: events, free/busy, incremental sync with sync tokens, push notifications via watch channels, and Meet links via conferenceData.
use_when: Two-way sync between the CRM and the client's Google calendar
Creating meetings with a Meet link from the app
avoid_when: Read-only sharing to many people; an ICS feed is simpler
integrate: Follow docs/calendars/01-integration-playbook.md: OAuth scopes, sync tokens, watch channels
Use the googleapis npm package from a server route; never call it from the browser with a secret
repos.learn_from: Sync tokens plus push channels means you never poll.

repos.name: Cal.com
repos.summary: Open scheduling platform: booking pages, availability rules, round-robin, embeds and calendar sync. Hosted or self-hosted.
use_when: Clients should book discovery calls themselves
You want an embeddable booking widget instead of building one
avoid_when: Self-hosting it just for one booking link; use the hosted version or a Calendly link
integrate: Embed the booking page with its embed snippet or React embed
Receive bookings by webhook into the CRM (creates or updates the client)
Check folder-level licenses before copying any code
repos.learn_from: Booking = availability rules + free/busy + a confirmation step. That's the whole Booking slots style.

repos.name: ical-generator
repos.summary: Generates ICS calendar files and feeds in Node. The quickest way to let anyone subscribe to your app's events.
use_when: 'Add to calendar' buttons
A private subscribe link for the client's follow-ups
avoid_when: Two-way sync; use the provider API
integrate: npm i ical-generator
Serve from a route like /api/calendar/[token].ics with a long random token
Set a stable UID per event so updates replace instead of duplicating
repos.learn_from: A stable UID is what makes calendar updates work everywhere.

repos.name: ical.js
repos.summary: Parses and writes iCalendar (ICS) and vCard, with time zones and recurrence. Used by Thunderbird and Nextcloud.
use_when: Importing ICS files or invites into the app
Expanding recurring events from a CalDAV server
avoid_when: You only need to generate feeds; ical-generator is simpler
integrate: npm i ical.js
ICAL.parse → new ICAL.Component → iterate vevent
Use its recurrence iterator for expanding occurrences in a date range
repos.learn_from: Always expand recurrence for the visible range only, never forever.

repos.name: rrule.js
repos.summary: Recurrence rules (RFC 5545 RRULE) in JS, with plain-English output like 'every week on Monday'.
use_when: Repeating follow-ups ('every 2 weeks') stored as an RRULE string
Showing a human description of a repeat rule
avoid_when: Time zone-heavy recurrence; check DST behavior or use ical.js
integrate: npm i rrule
Store the RRULE string in the database, expand on read for the visible range
rule.toText() for the label in the UI
repos.learn_from: Store the rule, not the occurrences.
